title: Plan
description: The complete description of what the system intends to do, and the sole contract between the Python planner (steps 1-8) and the Rust executor (steps 9-10). See docs/design-spec.md sections 3.5 and 5.3. Immutable once written: a superseded plan gets status='superseded', it is never edited.

schema_version.description: Semver of THIS schema. The executor refuses a plan whose major version it does not know rather than best-effort parsing it (design spec section 0.3, fail closed).

created_at.description: Wall-clock time the plan was written. Never used for decisions - see as_of.

as_of.description: The decision timestamp: the close of the newest bar the plan is allowed to have seen. Every feature and score in this plan is point-in-time as of here. Replaying the planner with this as_of must reproduce this plan.

mode.description: dry: never executable, produced by backtest or by `plan --dry-run`. live: eligible for execute_plan.

quote_currency.description: The currency NAV, weights and costs are denominated in.

gross_exposure.description: Sum of |weight| across positions, as a fraction of NAV.

benchmark_beta.description: Portfolio beta against the configured benchmark (BTC for crypto, SPY for equities). Null until a beta estimate exists.

provenance.description: Everything needed to re-derive this plan. If a plan cannot be reproduced from its inputs plus these versions, that is a bug, not a limitation (design spec section 5.1).

constructor.description: The constructor that actually produced these weights.

constructor_requested.description: The constructor that was asked for. Differs from `constructor` when a fallback fired (e.g. mvo did not converge). A silent unrecorded fallback makes a backtest uninterpretable, so this field is required, not optional.

model_id.description: Set only when an LLM-derived feature contributed. Null otherwise.

inputs_hash.description: Content hash of the bars and features this plan was computed from.

universe_size.description: Number of eligible assets at as_of. The completeness gate compares this against the expected floor.

targets.description: The desired portfolio. Complete: an asset absent from this list has a target weight of zero.

weight.description: Signed fraction of NAV. Negative means short.

conviction.description: The signal score that drove this weight, carried for attribution.

current.description: Positions as observed at the venue at as_of - the baseline the diff was taken against. Recorded so a stale plan can be detected before execution.

orders.description: The minimal set of orders that moves current to targets. Empty whenever status is rejected.

qty.description: Absolute base-asset quantity, always positive. Direction is carried by `side`.

reason.description: Why this order exists. `exit` and `reduce` are the only reasons permitted to run while trading is paused.

risk_report.description: The section 6 evaluation. A plan is accepted only if every hard limit passed - the risk layer rejects a plan whole, never partially.

cost_estimate.description: Estimated cost of executing this plan. Fed into the constructor's objective (design spec section 6.1), not merely reported. Compared against realised cost after execution.

warnings.description: Non-fatal disclosures that must be surfaced above any number derived from this plan: degenerate factors, unenforced rules, inadequate sample. Reported first, before results (design spec section 11).

allOf.description: A rejected plan carries no orders. Nothing downstream should have to remember this.
An accepted plan passed every hard limit.

asset.description: Canonical asset id, venue-independent. Venue symbol mapping lives in the adapter, never in a plan.

decimal.description: An exact decimal, carried as a string. Money and weights are never JSON numbers here: a JSON number is an IEEE double on both sides of this contract, and rounding that silently differs between Python and Rust is exactly the drift this schema exists to prevent.
